newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: U.S. agency grants Zambia $7 mln in new aid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency grants Zambia $7 mln in new aid.

text.p: The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) on Tuesday committed $7 million to four existing development projects in Zambia, effectively lifting a freeze on aid to the country.

The United States was among Western governments which tightened aid flows to Zambia last year in protest against constitutional changes enforced by the government before general elections last November.
Seven parties boycotted the polls, which were won by President Frederick Chiluba's Movement for Multiparty Democracy.

U.S. Ambassador Arlene Render and Zambian Finance Minister Ronald Penza signed agreements for the fresh aid, aimed at farm sector liberalisation, privatisation, family planning and child health care in the capital Lusaka.
At a donor meeting on Zambia earlier in July, donors said they were satisfied with the government's economic reforms, including its privatisation programme, and would ease restrictions on aid flows.

Render said the privatisation support project was a six-year $20 million programme which began in 1992. "The current additional $2 million completes funding of the project," Render told reporters at the signing ceremony.

She said the agricultural liberalisation project was a five-year programme worth $23 million which began in 1994, aimed at increasing the ability of rural farmers to participate in the market economy.
The new funding of $1.2 million brings the total USAID contribution to the programme to $8.2 million.
The five-year $20 million family planning services project, dating from 1993, is being boosted by an additional $1.8 million.

Render said the child health care project, worth $20 million over five years, was designed to increase the coverage and quality of child health care. "The current funding provides $2 million, bringing the amount funded to date to $7.5 million," she said.
The Zambian government has said it needs $200 million in balance of payments support and about $275 million in project financing in 1997.
